items.title: FreeBSDにおける複数の脆弱性
items.body: TLS 1.3は、復号化されたペイロードの最後のゼロでないバイトとして実際のレコードタイプを埋め込み、その後にゼロパディングが続く場合があります。内部レコードタイプを検索するコードにオフバイワンのバグがあり、無効なフレームによってこのバグが引き起こされるとアンダーフローが発生し、その後条件なしにNULLポインタ参照が行われてカーネルパニックを引き起こします。リモートのTLS 1.3ピアは、特別に細工されたレコードを送信することでカーネルパニックを引き起こせるため、サービス拒否（DoS）状態を招く可能性があります。

items.title: FreeBSDにおける通信チャネルの不適切な宛名の指定に関する脆弱性
items.body: 未接続ソケットのIPv6 UDP送信経路は、ループバック宛先アドレスをjailのプライマリIPv6アドレスに書き換えるjailポリシーを適用していませんでした。そのため、クラシック（非VNET）jail内のプロセスは、ホストのIPv6ループバックアドレスで待機しているサービスにUDPデータグラムを送信でき、jailのネットワーク分離が回避される可能性があります。

items.title: FreeBSDにおける削除された特権に対する不適切なチェックに関する脆弱性
items.body: fdescfs(4) が "nodup" オプション付きでジュール内にマウントされている場合、/dev/fd/N を開くと、FD_RESOLVE_BENEATH やディスクリプター N の Capsicum ケイパビリティ権限が継承されていないディスクリプターが返されます。別のジュールからディレクトリファイルディスクリプターを受け取ったジュール内のプロセスは、これらの手法を利用してジュールのファイルシステムルート制限を回避できます。

items.title: FreeBSDにおける削除された特権に対する不適切なチェックに関する脆弱性
items.body: renameat(2) は、そのディレクトリ引数に対して FD_RESOLVE_BENEATH を適用していませんでした。これにより、監獄（jail）内のプロセスが制限されたディスクリプタに相対的なディレクトリ名の変更を行い、fchdir(2) を使って監獄のルートを脱出できる可能性がありました。この操作は、ディレクトリが監獄のルートからもアクセス可能なファイルシステム上に存在している必要があります。別の監獄からディレクトリのファイルディスクリプタを受け取った監獄内のプロセスは、これらの手法を用いて監獄のファイルシステムルートの制限を回避できます。

items.title: FreeBSDにおける複数の脆弱性
items.body: SCM_RIGHTSによるファイルディスクリプタの転送時に、FD_RESOLVE_BENEATHフラグが保持されませんでした。そのため、プロセスはUnixドメインソケットを通じて自身にディスクリプタを送信することで、この制限を解除できました。別のjailからディレクトリのファイルディスクリプタを受け取ったjail内のプロセスは、これらの手法を用いることでjailのファイルシステムルート制限を回避することが可能です。

items.title: FreeBSDにおける複数の脆弱性
items.body: PCMサンプル配列を拡張する必要がある場合、RACKスタックは16ビットの割り当てカウンターを倍増させます。繰り返し倍増するとカウンターがゼロに巻き戻り、ほぼゼロ長の割り当てが発生し、その後既存のサンプルが過小サイズのバッファにコピーされてしまいます。リモートのピアは確立された接続上で十分な数のACKを送信することでこの拡張をトリガーできます。リモート攻撃者がRACKスタックを使用するシステムにTCP接続を確立できる場合、カーネルヒープに約512KBの境界外書き込みを引き起こし、カーネルパニックを誘発する可能性があります。

items.body: オーディオチャンネルのバッファサイズを変更する必要がある場合、sound(4)ドライバはバッファがメモリマップされていないことを確認し、その後チャンネルロックを解除して新しいバッファを割り当てます。この間に別のスレッドでmmap(2)呼び出しが完了する可能性があり、その後リサイズ処理は再確認せずにマップされたバッファを解放してしまいます。サウンドデバイスへのアクセス権を持つ特権のないローカルユーザーは、このレースコンディションを悪用してカーネル内でuse-after-freeを引き起こし、権限昇格を行う可能性があります。

items.body:
Improper Authentication vulnerability in Apache Camel OAuth component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.11.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The camel-oauth processors that guard a route did not stop the exchange when authentication could not be completed. Where a failure to establish an authenticated session should have terminated routing and returned an error to the caller, the processors fell through and returned control to the route, so the request continued to the protected endpoint as though authentication had succeeded. The effect is a fail-open authentication guard: an unauthenticated caller reached whatever the route did next. The condition is reached on the ordinary request path of a route configured to require OAuth, and needs no special configuration or prior access on the caller's part.



Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.18.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.18.5. Users on the 4.22.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.22.1. The processors now stop the exchange and set the appropriate error status whenever an authenticated session cannot be established, so a failed authentication no longer reaches the protected part of the route. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, place an explicit authorization check after the OAuth processor rather than relying on it to halt the exchange, and verify that the route stops on failure.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Apache Camel Azure Files component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.0.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The Camel remote-file consumers poll a directory on a remote server and build the absolute remote path of each file by concatenating the configured directory with the file name reported in the server's directory listing. That concatenation (FtpUtils.absoluteFilePath and GenericFileConsumer) applied no lexical normalization and no check that the result stayed inside the directory being polled, and the resulting path became the operand for every subsequent remote operation on the file: retrieval (FtpOperations.retrieveFile / SftpOperations, reached from GenericFileConsumer where the retrieve name is taken verbatim from GenericFile.getAbsoluteFilePath), deletion when delete=true (GenericFileDeleteProcessStrategy), and renaming when move, preMove, moveFailed or readLock=rename is configured (GenericFileProcessStrategySupport and GenericFileRenameExclusiveReadLockStrategy). Neither isValidFile nor isMatched performed any containment check. Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Camel Spring Redis component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 2.11.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



RedisConfiguration.getSerializer lazily built a bare JdkSerializationRedisSerializer whenever no serializer option was configured, and that instance was used for every read the component performs. Spring's implementation delegates through DeserializingConverter to DefaultDeserializer, which reads the bytes with a ConfigurableObjectInputStream and installs no java.io.ObjectInputFilter on the stream, so an arbitrary serialized class graph was materialised and its readObject method executed. The component never constructed a java.io.ObjectInputStream itself, which is why earlier passes over the Camel codebase for unfiltered Java deserialization did not reach it. ReplicatedHazelcastAggregationRepository extends HazelcastAggregationRepository but overrides doStart() without calling super.doStart(), keeping its own copy of the bootstrap block, and therefore never received the filter: a route using it without supplying a hazelcastInstance starts a Hazelcast member that deserializes values read from the backing ReplicatedMap with no class restriction. HazelcastDefaultComponent#getOrCreateHzClientInstance() builds its own ClientConfig when hazelcastMode=client is selected and neither a referenced ClientConfig nor hazelcastConfigUri is supplied, and likewise applied no filter, so client-mode endpoints behaved differently from node-mode endpoints for an otherwise identical configuration. In both cases an attacker able to publish into the Hazelcast cluster that the affected instance is attached to can cause a serialized Java object of their choosing to be deserialized inside Hazelcast's own serialization layer, before Camel processes the exchange, resulting in remote code execution. Hazelcast clusters have neither authentication nor TLS enabled by default. items.title: CVE-2026-112192 - MISP contains a vulnerability in the handling of module plugin settings. When th...
items.body:
MISP contains a vulnerability in the handling of module plugin settings. When the server rebuilds module-supplied settings for API consumption, it drops the redacted and cli_only flags that a module declares in its own configuration metadata.

As a result:

- A module that marks a setting (such as an API key) as redacted still has its value returned in full by the servers/getSetting and servers/serverSettingsEdit endpoints, exposing sensitive credentials to any authenticated user who can read server settings.

- A module that marks a setting as cli_only (intended to be editable only via the command-line interface) can still be modified through the web API, bypassing the intended access restriction.

An authenticated user with access to server settings can therefore read sensitive module credentials and modify settings that the module author intended to restrict to CLI-only access.

Affected: <2.5.48

items.title: CVE-2026-112188 - MISP contains a vulnerability in its server settings lookup mechanism that allow...
items.body:
MISP contains a vulnerability in its server settings lookup mechanism that allows an authenticated user to retrieve sensitive configuration data that should have been redacted.

The settings lookup function resolves a dotted setting name to a node in the configuration tree. When a branch name (such as Security, MISP, or Plugin) is supplied instead of a specific leaf setting, the function returns the entire sub-tree. Because a branch node does not carry a redaction flag, the redaction check in the settings retrieval endpoint is bypassed, and the full branch contents are returned to the caller. This exposes sensitive values including the security salt, Redis connection passwords, and plugin API keys.

A second endpoint that edits server settings similarly reads the entire configuration store when a branch name is resolved, returning all settings to the caller.

The impact is disclosure of sensitive server configuration secrets to any user who can access the server settings endpoints.

Affected versions: <2.5.48.

在 openGauss-server的 src/common/backend/utils/adt/genfile.cpp 模块中，内置函数 pg_read_binary_file_blocks() 存在权限校验逻辑缺陷。该函数在入口处仅校验了起始块号（startBlockNum）和块数量（blockCount）的范围，随后直接调用底层文件读取例程 ReadBinaryFileBlocksFirstCall()。该底层例程仅执行了路径规范化检查以及针对 .. 路径遍历和数据目录边界的基本检查，缺失了对调用者数据库权限（如 SELECT 权限）的校验。此外，辅助函数 is_row_data_file() 也仅用于识别文件形态，未包含权限检查。因此，任何拥有普通数据库连接权限的用户，只要能够通过 pg_relation_filepath() 等函数获取到目标表的底层关系文件路径（例如压缩数据的 _compress 文件路径），即可无需具备该表的 SELECT 权限，直接读取表数据的二进制块。

items.title: CVE-2026-111441 - 在 openGauss-server 的 src/gausskernel/cbb/utils/hll/hll.cpp 中，内置函数 HllObjectUnpac...
items.body: 在 openGauss-server 的 src/gausskernel/cbb/utils/hll/hll.cpp 中，内置函数 HllObjectUnpack() 存在长度校验缺陷。该函数从用户提供的 packed HLL 解析 lenUsed 与 lenTotal 后，仅检查输入长度足以覆盖 HLL_HEAD_SIZE + lenUsed，随后按 lenTotal 分配缓冲区、按 lenUsed 调用 memcpy_s() 拷贝输入，既未校验 lenTotal >= lenUsed，也将 memcpy_s() 目标大小写成 lenUsed 而非实际分配的 lenTotal，导致安全拷贝无法拦截越界写。hll_in()、hll_print()、hll_cardinality() 等 SQL 入口会走同一解包路径。因此，普通数据库连接用户只需构造 lenTotal 小于 lenUsed 的畸形 packed HLL（例如经 ::hll 进入 hll_in()），即可触发服务端堆越界写，存在内存破坏风险。此问题随 packed HLL 解包函数 HllObjectUnpack() 进入代码，v2.1.0 起即存在。受影响版本包括 2.1.0、3.0.x、3.1.x、5.0.x、5.1.0、6.0.x，以及 7.0.0-RC1、7.0.0-RC2、7.0.0-RC3。该问题已在 7.0.0-LTS 版本修复，通过在 HllObjectUnpack() 中补齐 lenUsed <= lenTotal 校验，并将 memcpy_s() 的目标大小改为实际分配的 lenTotal。修复 PR 见 https://gitcode.com/opengauss/openGauss-server/pull/9380 。

items.title: CVE-2026-103091 - Missing Authorization (CWE-862) and Initialization of a Resource with an Insecur...
items.body: Missing Authorization (CWE-862) and Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default (CWE-1188) in the MCP proxy (HandleStreamPassThrough in mcp_service.go) and OIDC registration flow (GET /info and POST /register in internal/controlplane/server.go) in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.8 allow a remote attacker to self-enroll into the mesh and invoke arbitrary tools across all connected MCP backend nodes. Because GET /info publicly discloses OIDC configuration, POST /register auto-enrolls any valid OIDC token holder without claim filtering or ban checks, and the default policy binds sam:system:authenticated to wildcard services and targets, an attacker can obtain a mesh credential with full read, write, and execution access on backend services. Users should upgrade to version 0.1.0-alpha.9 or later, which enforces a fail-closed default policy, explicit policy-binding requirements on enrollment, and ban checks.

items.title: CVE-2026-102503 - Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-306) and Missing Authorization...
items.body: Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-306) and Missing Authorization (CWE-862) in the /libp2p-http ingress server (StartIngressServer in cmd/sam-node/node.go) in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.2 allow an unauthenticated remote libp2p peer to bypass Biscuit capability policy enforcement and invoke arbitrary registered backend services (including command/stdio-backed MCP servers, A2A, and inference endpoints). While the MCP protocol stream handler enforces WithBiscuitAuth and Authorize checks, the parallel /libp2p-http ingress routes requests directly to backend service handlers without verifying a Biscuit token or mesh enrollment. Users should upgrade to version 0.1.0-alpha.3 or later.

items.title: Linux Foundationのbackstage/plugin-scaffolder-backend-module-confluence-to-markdown等の複数製品における複数の脆弱性
items.body: Backstageは開発者向けポータルを構築するためのオープンフレームワークです。バージョン0.3.25より前の@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-backend-module-confluence-to-markdownパッケージには、ConfluenceからMarkdownへのスキャフォルダーモジュールにおいて不適切な入力検証の脆弱性があります。ConfluenceからMarkdownへのスキャフォルダーモジュールの入力検証が不十分であるため、攻撃者がテンプレート実行中のファイル書き込み操作に影響を与える可能性があります。この脆弱性を悪用するには、Backstageユーザーが攻撃者に操作されたConfluenceコンテンツを処理するテンプレートを実行しなければなりません。この問題はバージョン0.3.25で修正されています。

items.title: Linux Foundationのbackstage/plugin-scaffolder-backend-module-confluence-to-markdown等の複数製品におけるパストラバーサルの脆弱性
items.body: Backstageは、開発者ポータルを構築するためのオープンフレームワークです。バージョン0.3.25以前の@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-backend-module-confluence-to-markdownパッケージには、不適切なリポジトリパス検証の脆弱性が存在していました。この脆弱性はスキャフォルダーバックエンドモジュールに影響を及ぼします。認証されたユーザーが対象のテンプレートを実行し、そのリポジトリファイルの場所を制御できる場合、生成されたコンテンツがタスクの作業スペース外の、Backstageバックエンドプロセスが書き込み可能な場所に書き込まれる可能性があります。この問題はバージョン0.3.25で修正されています。

items.title: Linux Foundationのbackstage/plugin-kubernetes-backend等の複数製品における複数の脆弱性
items.body: Backstageは開発者向けポータルを構築するためのオープンフレームワークです。バージョン0.21.9以前の@backstage/plugin-kubernetes-backendパッケージには、Kubernetesリソースクエリにおける機密情報の漏洩の脆弱性があります。標準的なKubernetesリソースの読み取り権限を持つ認証済みユーザーは、Kubernetesプラグインによってマスクされるよう設計されている機密値を取得できる可能性があり、接続されたクラスタ内に保持されている資格情報やその他の機密情報が露呈する恐れがあります。漏洩の範囲は、Backstageのサービスアカウントが読み取り許可を持ち、かつ対象となるカタログエンティティのネームスペースおよびラベルセレクターに一致するリソースに限定されます。クラスタの認証情報がこれらのリソースへの読み取りアクセスを付与していないデプロイメントは影響を受けません。この問題はバージョン0.21.9で修正されています。

items.title: Linux Foundationのbackstage/plugin-search-backend-module-elasticsearch等の複数製品における複数の脆弱性
items.body: Backstageは、開発者ポータルを構築するためのオープンフレームワークです。@backstage/plugin-search-backendのバージョン2.1.6未満および@backstage/plugin-search-backend-module-elasticsearchのバージョン1.8.7未満では、検索エンジンの権限フィルタリングがポリシーで拒否されたドキュメントを返してしまう可能性がありました。認証されたBackstageユーザーが検索ドキュメントタイプに対してDENYポリシーの対象となっている場合に、permission.enabledがtrueに設定されている環境で、ElasticsearchまたはOpenSearchバックエンドを使用すると、不正な結果を受け取る事態が発生していました。この問題は、@backstage/plugin-search-backend 2.1.6および@backstage/plugin-search-backend-module-elasticsearch 1.8.7で修正されています。

items.title: Linux Foundationのbackstage/plugin-kubernetes-backend等の複数製品における複数の脆弱性
items.body: Backstageは開発者ポータルを構築するためのオープンフレームワークです。バージョン0.21.8より前の@backstage/plugin-kubernetes-backendパッケージには、非推奨のkubernetesサービスエンドポイントにおける不適切なエンティティ検証の脆弱性が存在します。Kubernetesの読み取り権限を持つ認証済みユーザーは、巧妙に作成されたエンティティデータを非推奨のサービスエンドポイントに提供することで、本来の範囲を超えたKubernetesワークロードデータにアクセスできてしまいます。影響範囲は、構成されたクラスター全体のKubernetesオブジェクトメタデータへの読み取り専用アクセスに限定されています。この問題はバージョン0.21.8で修正されています。

items.body: Apache CXFのJAX-RS XMLセキュリティモジュールには、暗号署名の不適切な検証に関する脆弱性があります。JAX-RS XML署名インターセプター（XmlSigInHandler、XmlSigInInterceptor、およびストリーミングのXmlSecInInterceptor）は、アプリケーションに渡されるXMLが署名で保護されていることを適切に保証していませんでした。攻撃者は信頼されたキーで署名された任意のドキュメントを取得し、それを署名されていないコンテンツで包むことができ、その結果アプリケーションは当該コンテンツを署名済みと誤認識してしまいます。ユーザーには、この問題を修正したバージョン4.2.4、4.1.9、または3.6.13にアップグレードすることを推奨します。

items.title: Doclingにおけるパストラバーサルの脆弱性
items.body: Doclingは、多様なフォーマットを解析し、生成AIエコシステムとの統合を提供することで、ドキュメント処理を簡素化します。バージョン2.107.0から2.120.3までの間、docling/backend/opendocument_backend.pyは、参照された部分がドキュメントアーカイブ内に存在しない場合に、draw:image要素のxlink:href属性値をファイルシステムパスとして使用していました。_image_ref_from_odf_image関数は、スキームチェックや抽出ディレクトリの制限、他のバックエンドで使用されるenable_local_fetch設定なしに、その攻撃者が制御可能なパスを読み込んでいました。Pillowが画像としてデコードできる読み取り可能なファイルは変換後の出力に埋め込まれ、他の既存パスは読み取り試行により区別されていました。この問題はバージョン2.120.3で修正されました。

items.title: vLLMにおけるリソースの枯渇に関する脆弱性
items.body: vLLMは大規模言語モデルの推論およびサービングエンジンです。バージョン0.30.0以前では、Rustフロントエンドのtrack_http_metricsミドルウェアが、登録されたルートに到達するリクエストの生のHTTPメソッドトークンをPrometheusのラベルとして記録していました。認証されていない攻撃者が/tokenizeのような保護されていないルートに任意のユニークなメソッドトークンを送信すると、PrometheusのFamily::get_or_create関数がカウンターおよびヒストグラムのラベルセットを恒久的に作成し続けます。これらのラベルセットによってプロセスのメモリ使用量が増加し、/metricsレスポンスが肥大化してサービスまたは監視経路が枯渇する可能性があります。この問題はバージョン0.30.0で修正されています。

items.title: vLLMにおけるリソースの枯渇に関する脆弱性
items.body: vLLMは大規模言語モデルの推論およびサービスエンジンとして機能します。バージョン0.30.0以前では、呼び出し元がrequest-levelのmedia_io_kwargsフィールドを使用してGLMGAビデオバックエンドを選択し、fpsおよびmax_framesオプションに対して厳格な上限なしに大きな値を指定できました。GLMGAは攻撃者がサイズの大きい事前デコードフレームインデックスリストを構築および重複排除できるようにし、コンパクトなリクエストと非常に小さな有効ビデオに対して、共有メディアロード実行環境で過剰なCPU時間とメモリを消費させることを可能にしていました。この問題はバージョン0.30.0で修正されています。

items.title: Apache Software FoundationのApache CXFにおける制限またはスロットリング無しのリソースの割り当てに関する脆弱性
items.body: Apache CXFにおいて、multipart/MTOMの添付パートヘッダーのパーサーは、設定されたattachment-max-header-size（デフォルト300文字）およびattachment-headers-max-count（デフォルト500）の制限を完全には適用していませんでした。サイズ制限は各物理行にのみ適用されており、継続行から構築されたヘッダー値や繰り返されるヘッダーの結合値には適用されていませんでした。カウント制限は異なるヘッダー名の数に対してのみチェックされており、ヘッダー行の総数にはチェックされていませんでした。リモートの認証されていない攻撃者が非常に大きな折りたたまれたまたは繰り返されるパートヘッダーを含むmultipartリクエストを送信することが可能であり、これによりサーバーは無制限にメモリを割り当ててサービス拒否（DoS）を引き起こす可能性があります。ユーザーは本問題を修正したバージョン4.2.4、4.1.9、または3.6.13にアップグレードすることを推奨します。

items.title: Apache Software FoundationのApache CXFにおけるホストの不一致による証明書の検証に関する脆弱性
items.body: Apache CXFにおいて、NettyベースのHTTPクライアントトランスポート（cxf-rt-transports-http-netty-client）は、サーバーのTLS証明書に記載されたホスト名が呼び出し先のホストと一致しているかを検証していませんでした。これはHTTP/1.1およびHTTP/2の両方に該当し、disableCNCheckがデフォルト値のfalseのままでも同様でした。証明書チェーンは設定された信頼ストアに対して検証されていましたが、エンドポイントの正当性は検証されていませんでした。通信を傍受できる攻撃者は、クライアントが信頼する任意の証明書（攻撃者が管理するドメインに対して公開発行された証明書など）を提示して、ターゲットサービスをなりすますことが可能でした。これにより、認証情報を含むメッセージのやり取りを読み取ったり改ざんしたりすることができました。ユーザーには、この問題が修正されたバージョン4.2.4、4.1.9、または3.6.13へアップグレードすることを推奨します。

items.title: Apache Software FoundationのApache CXFにおけるDTD の再帰的なエンティティ参照の不適切な制限に関する脆弱性
items.body: デフォルトでは、StaxUtils は XML ドキュメント内の要素の総数や文字の総数に制限を設けていませんでした。そのため、非常に大きなリクエストは、特に CXF が入力から DOM を構築する場合（例：SAAJ や WS-Security）において、パース中に多くのメモリと CPU を消費し、リクエストサイズ制限が設定されていないとサービス拒否（DoS）を引き起こす可能性がありました。現在、両方の制限にはデフォルト値が設定されています。最大要素数は 100 × maxChildElements（デフォルトで 5,000,000）であり、最大ドキュメントサイズは 256M 文字です。より大きなドキュメントを処理するアプリケーションは、org.apache.cxf.stax.maxElementCount および org.apache.cxf.stax.maxXMLCharacters プロパティでこれらの制限を引き上げることができます。ユーザーには、この問題を修正したバージョン 4.2.4、4.1.9、もしくは 3.6.13 へアップグレードすることを推奨します。

items.title: CVE-2026-112112 - An IPv6 FlowSpec validation bypass in the CZ.NIC BIRD Internet Routing Daemon al...
items.body: An IPv6 FlowSpec validation bypass in the CZ.NIC BIRD Internet Routing Daemon allows an established BGP peer to inject FlowSpec rules matching destinations outside the address space authorized by the unicast-route validation procedure. With validation enabled on the receiving flow6 channel, BIRD fails to reject a destination prefix component with a nonzero offset, contrary to RFC 8956 section 5. It validates a reconstructed prefix with zero-filled skipped bits, although the original FlowSpec component can match a broader set of IPv6 addresses. Given a suitable unicast route from the peer, the rule can pass validation and, where export policy permits, be propagated to downstream peers. Downstream enforcement may cause unauthorized traffic filtering or redirection.

items.body: The Bootstrap Shortcodes plugin for WordPress before 3.4.6 is vulnerable to stored XSS via the id attribute of the [bs_tcontent] shortcode. The bs_tcontent() shortcode handler in inc/bs_tabs.php emits the id attribute value into an unquoted HTML attribute. esc_attr() is applied, but it does not encode space characters, so a space in the supplied value terminates the attribute and any following text is parsed as additional HTML attributes, including JavaScript event handlers. This allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to inject arbitrary web script that executes in the browser of any user who views the page and interacts with the injected element.

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: ufs: core: Keep internal commands dispatchable during error handling

Commit 08b12cda6c44 ("scsi: ufs: core: Switch to scsi_get_internal_cmd()")
switched UFS internal commands to allocate requests on
hba->host->pseudo_sdev->request_queue, which shares the host tagset with
regular LUNs.

During error recovery, ufshcd_err_handling_prepare() calls
blk_mq_quiesce_tagset(&hba->host->tag_set), marking all queues in the
tagset as quiesced, including pseudo_sdev->request_queue. When
ufshcd_verify_dev_init() subsequently issues internal commands (e.g. NOP
OUT UPIU) via blk_execute_rq(), blk_mq_run_hw_queue() skips running the
quiesced queue, resulting in an unrecoverable circular wait deadlock.

Keep quiescing the tagset and unquiesce the pseudo SCSI device on top of
that, so internal commands stay dispatchable while the logical units remain
quiesced. Re-quiesce the pseudo device before unquiescing the tagset so
that quiesce_depth stays balanced.

Clock scaling and ufshcd_pause_command_processing() are unaffected: they
keep quiescing the whole tagset, internal commands included.

perf/core: Fix NULL pmu_ctx passed to pmu->sched_task()

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: SEV: Free have_run_cpus during VM destruction even if VM is no longer SEV

Unconditionally free SEV's "have run CPUs" cpumask in the VM destroy path,
i.e. even for what appear to be non-SEV VMs, as an SEV VM becomes a non-SEV
VM if its state is intra-host migrated.  Alternatively, the mask could be
freed in sev_migrate_from() when "converting" the source VM, but that gets
annoying because ideally KVM would nullify the mask to guard against UAF,
and nullifying the mask would need be conditioned on CPUMASK_OFFSTACK=y.

Freeing the mask during sev_migrate_from() is also not robust against other
KVM bugs, though that's kind of a moot point since any such bugs would show
up even if sev->active is never set.  I.e. KVM must get that side of things
correct.  But, that's not a great reason to add more code just to make
things marginally less robust.

KVM: SEV: D...
items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: SEV: Do cache maintenance on the source VM during intra-host migration

Manually perform cache maintenance on the source VM during intra-host
migration to ensure no stale data is left in CPU caches after the VM is
destroyed.  Because the source VM is "converted" to a non-SEV VM, KVM's
memory reclaim flows won't trigger cache maintenance, e.g. when all guest
memory is reclaimed in response to detaching from the mmu_notifier.

Note, relying on the destination VM to do cache maintenance isn't an option
as KVM doesn't require identical guest memory configurations, i.e. the
source VM may have access to memory that the destination VM does not.
Enforcing equivalent memory configurations is infeasible, as it would
require a *deep* comparison of memslots, e.g. to verify that not only are
the memslot identical, but what the memslots point at is also identical.

KVM: arm64: Fix AArch32 DBGBXVR<n> handling

The consolidation of the breakpoint and watchpoint register accessors

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: arm64: Fix spurious warning for benign stage 2 teardown race

kvmtool was used to establish an L1 guest with 8 CPUs and 8 GiB of RAM, an
L2 guest with 4 CPUs and 4 GiB of RAM and an L3 guest with 2 CPUs and 2 GiB
of RAM, all of which was then exited.

Under memory pressure in the L0 host warnings were observed due to
migration triggered by compaction:

WARNING: arch/arm64/kvm/mmu.c:336 at __unmap_stage2_range+0x64/0x80,
CPU#5: kcompactd0/66

Which was, in turn, triggered by an MMU notifier for the host invalidation:

mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start()
  -> ... -> kvm_mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start()
    -> kvm_mmu_unmap_gfn_range()
      -> kvm_unmap_gfn_range()
        -> kvm_nested_s2_unmap()
          -> kvm_stage2_unmap_range()
            -> __unmap_stage2_range()
               -> stage2_apply_range()
       	       <- -EINVAL, triggering a WARN_ON()

Racing with L0's teardown of stage 2 page tables:

exit_mm()
  -> mmput()
    -> __mmput()
      -> exit_mmap()
        -> mmu_notifier_release()
	  -> ... -> kvm_mmu_notifier_release()
            -> kvm_flush_shadow_all()
              -> kvm_arch_flush_shadow_all()
	        -> kvm_free_stage2_pgd()
		  -> [ acquire kvm->mmu_lock for write ]
		  -> mmu->pgt = NULL [ among other tasks ]
		  -> [ release kvm->mmu_lock for write ]

It turns out there is a benign race resulting in a spurious warning:

	Thread A - notify: migration   | Thread B - notify: release
	-------------------------------|---------------------------------
	< kvm->mmu_lock held >         |
	stage2_apply_range()           |
	  get mmu->pgt, check !NULL    |
	  ...                          | kvm_arch_flush_shadow_all()
	  cond_resched_rwlock_write(); |   < contend, sleep kvm->mmu_lock >
	< drop kvm->mmu_lock >         |   < acquire kvm->mmu_lock>
                                       |   ...
				       |   kvm_free_stage2_pgd()

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: arm64: nv: Fix null ptr deref on nested wp/unmap, teardown race

Commit 7270cc9157f4 ("KVM: arm64: nv: Handle VNCR_EL2 invalidation from MMU
notifiers") introduced VNCR_EL2 invalidation in both kvm_nested_s2_unmap()
and kvm_nested_s2_wp().

However at the point of this being performed concurrent stage 2 teardown of
a nested guest can cause kvm->arch.mmu.pgt to be set to NULL.

This happens in kvm_flush_shadow_all() -> kvm_arch_flush_shadow_all() ->
kvm_free_stage2_pgd() and is performed under the kvm->mmu_lock.

Commit ec14c272408a ("KVM: arm64: nv: Unmap/flush shadow stage 2 page
tables") introduced the teardown of the entire nested MMU range, which then
invokes stage2_apply_range() with resched=true:

mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start()
  -> ... -> kvm_mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start()
    -> kvm_mmu_unmap_gfn_range()
      -> kvm_unmap_gfn_range()
        -> kvm_nested_s2_unmap()
          -> kvm_stage2_unmap_range()
            -> __unmap_stage2_range()
                -> stage2_apply_range()

This means that stage2_apply_range() can drop the kvm->mmu_lock and thus
concurrent progress can be made in lockstep with
kvm_arch_flush_shadow_all().

If kvm_arch_flush_shadow_all() advances ahead of stage2_apply_range() and
completes its operation it guarantees a NULL pointer deref.

Since kvm_free_stage2_pgd() is performed under the kvm->mmu_lock this will
either be observed NULL or not and serialised against
kvm_free_stage2_pgd().

Resolve the issue by abstracting the invalidation to a new function,
kvm_invalidate_vncr_ipa_all(), and check that the pgt is non-NULL before
dereferencing it.

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RISC-V: KVM: Serialize IMSIC attributes with vCPU migration

KVM device ioctls are not serialized against KVM_RUN. As a result,
kvm_riscv_aia_imsic_rw_attr() can snapshot the physical CPU and HGEI of
an IMSIC VS-file before a concurrent vCPU migration releases it.

The HGEI can then be allocated to another vCPU before imsic_vsfile_rw()
uses the stale tuple. A GET or SET attribute may consequently access the
new owner's interrupt file.

Serialize the entire IMSIC attribute operation with the target vCPU
mutex. This prevents the VS-file from being migrated and recycled until
the attribute access completes. Acquire the mutex killably so that the
device ioctl remains interruptible while waiting for KVM_RUN to finish.

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RISC-V: KVM: Synchronize hrtimer callback during teardown

The non-Sstc hrtimer callback clears next_set before its final uses of
the enclosing vCPU.  If teardown observes next_set as false while the
callback is still running, kvm_riscv_vcpu_timer_cancel() skips
hrtimer_cancel() and kvm_destroy_vcpus() can free the vCPU before the
callback enters kvm_riscv_vcpu_set_interrupt().

A guest can arm the timer with SBI TIME and request shutdown with SBI
legacy shutdown or SRST.  A VMM that honors KVM_EXIT_SYSTEM_EVENT and
destroys the VM supplies the teardown side of the race; no post-launch
host ioctl is needed to arm or request teardown.

On upstream master 62cc90241548, generic KASAN reported:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in do_raw_spin_lock
  Write of size 4 at addr ff60000005e58898

  kvm_riscv_vcpu_set_interrupt
  kvm_riscv_vcpu_hrtimer_expired
  __hrtimer_run_queues
  hrtimer_interrupt

The object was allocated by KVM_CREATE_VCPU and freed concurrently by:

  kvm_destroy_vcpus
  kvm_arch_destroy_vm
  kvm_destroy_vm
  __fput

For deterministic validation, I added mdelay(1000) immediately after
the existing next_set = false assignment.  This only widens the
existing post-clear callback window.  A no-delay trace build naturally
reached the callback-after-teardown-start/before-deinit ordering in 12
of 200 runs, but 1,500 stock-kernel stress iterations did not produce a
KASAN report, so natural reproduction is timing-sensitive.

Always invoke hrtimer_cancel() for an initialized timer.  Preserve the
existing -EINVAL result when the timer is no longer set, but only after
synchronizing with a running callback.

With this patch, hrtimer_cancel() blocked for the full widened callback
window before vCPU destruction.  KASAN reported no error in 100
fixed-and-widened runs or 200 fix-only timing-sweep runs.

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched_ext: Derive SCX_RQ_IN_WAKEUP from the core enqueue flags

schedule_deferred_locked() skips scheduling a deferred action while
SCX_RQ_IN_WAKEUP is set and relies on the task_woken_scx() call that follows
a wakeup enqueue to run it. enqueue_task_scx() sets the flag from the merged
enqueue flags, which include the flags stashed for a remote activation.
move_remote_task_to_local_dsq() thus sets SCX_RQ_IN_WAKEUP on the
destination rq when the moved task was woken up, although no
task_woken_scx() follows that activation.

An IMMED insert into a busy destination requests a local reenqueue during
that enqueue. The request gets linked but not scheduled and stays pending
until an unrelated wakeup or preemption on that CPU runs the deferred
actions. The IMMED task sits behind the running task in the meantime. If
nothing runs them before the scheduler is disabled, the request outlives the
scheduler and points into its freed per-cpu area, which the next scheduler
dereferences from run_deferred().

Test the core enqueue flags for the wakeup bit. Only the core's wakeup path
is followed by task_woken_scx().

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: hci_conn: fix CIS hold ownership on reuse

Commit 69997d50ec57 ("Bluetooth: ISO: handle bound CIS cleanup via
hci_conn") made hci_bind_cis() and hci_connect_cis() return a
connection with one hold for the ISO layer.  hci_bind_cis() currently
takes that hold only after configuring a CIS, so its BT_CONNECTED and
matching BT_BOUND paths return a bare lookup result.  Its configuration
failure path can likewise call hci_conn_drop() before taking a hold.

Take the hold before any state-dependent return or configuration error
so every successful return follows the documented ownership contract
and every error drop is balanced.

hci_connect_cis() also assumes hci_conn_link() always takes a new CIS
hold before dropping the one returned by hci_bind_cis().  However, the
helper returns an existing link without taking another hold.  In that
case, preserve the CIS hold for the caller and drop the redundant LE
hold because the existing link already owns its parent hold.  Returning
early also avoids changing an existing CIS back to BT_CONNECT.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: hci_sock: validate event length before filtering

is_filtered_packet() reads the event code from skb->data[0] without first
checking that the skb is nonempty. When an opcode filter is configured,
it also reads the command opcode at offsets 3 or 4 without checking that
a Command Complete or Command Status event is long enough.

hci_send_to_sock() invokes the filter before hci_event_packet() validates
the event header. A malformed event supplied by a controller or a vhci
device can therefore cause an out-of-bounds read.

Keep the unmasked event code for the opcode checks. The masked value is
needed for the 64-bit event bitmap, but using it to identify command events
aliases event codes above 0x3f. In particular, Synchronous Train Complete
(0x4f) was treated as Command Status (0x0f) even though its payload has no
opcode.

Reject actual command events that are too short for the field being
inspected. A truncated command event cannot match a configured opcode.

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: hci_sock: reject out-of-range OCF values

The raw HCI socket security filter has 128 OCF bits per supported OGF,
but masks the 10-bit OCF with 127 before looking up the command. An
unprivileged socket can therefore submit a reserved OCF that aliases an
allowlisted command modulo 128.

A conforming controller should reject reserved opcodes. Nevertheless,
the security decision must apply to the opcode that will actually be
sent, especially since controller-specific behavior is outside the host
stack's control.

Reject OCF values that cannot be represented by the security filter
instead of aliasing them onto an unrelated command.

Bluetooth: ISO: balance the parent hold in hci_bind_bis()

hci_conn_link() takes a lifetime reference to its parent with
hci_conn_get(), but only takes an operational hold on the child.
hci_conn_unlink() later balances both a hold and a reference on the
parent.

The SCO and CIS paths pass a parent acquired from a connect helper, so
it already has a hold. For an additional BIS, hci_bind_bis() obtains the
parent from hci_conn_hash_lookup_big(), which returns a bare pointer.
Unlinking the child then drops the parent's existing hold and can
schedule it for disconnection while its socket is still using it.

Take a hold on the parent before linking it and drop that hold if linking
fails. A successful link transfers the hold to hci_conn_unlink().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: ISO: release unused CIS holds after channel attach

hci_bind_cis() and hci_connect_cis() return one hci_conn hold for the
ISO layer.  A new channel association consumes that hold, which is
eventually released by iso_conn_free().

There are two cases where iso_chan_add() does not create an association:
it returns success when the socket is already attached to the same
iso_conn, and it returns -EBUSY when another socket is attached.  The
hold returned for the current call is unused in both cases.  This occurs
when deferred setup calls iso_connect_cis() again for its existing
socket, or when another socket attempts to reuse the CIS.

Detect the idempotent case while the connection is locked and release
the unused hold after iso_chan_add().  Also release it on -EBUSY.  Do not
drop it for other errors: a newly allocated iso_conn releases the
transferred hold when its last temporary reference is put.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: validate frame length before control and FCS access

l2cap_data_rcv() unpacks either a two-byte or four-byte control field
without first ensuring that it is present. A short ERTM or streaming-mode
frame can therefore cause an out-of-bounds read.

There is a second short-frame case when CRC16 is enabled. After the
control field is pulled, l2cap_check_fcs() subtracts two from skb->len
without checking it. If fewer than two bytes remain, the subtraction
wraps; skb_trim() leaves the buffer unchanged and the subsequent FCS
load reads past the logical end of the frame.

Validate that the frame contains both its control field and, when
enabled, its FCS before either field is accessed.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: mgmt: fix race in read_unconf_index_list()

read_unconf_index_list() counts unconfigured controllers before allocating
its response, then checks the device flags again while filling it.

hci_dev_list_lock stabilizes list membership, but it does not serialize the
per-device flags. During asynchronous controller setup, the worker can set
HCI_UNCONFIGURED and clear HCI_SETUP between the two passes. A controller
omitted from the allocation count can then become eligible for the fill
pass, causing an out-of-bounds write to rp->index[].

Allocate space for every device on hci_dev_list. Since list membership
cannot change while hci_dev_list_lock is held, the response remains large
enough regardless of flag transitions. The reported count and response
length still include only eligible unconfigured controllers.

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: RFCOMM: fix NULL dereference of dlc->session in RFCOMM_CONNINFO

The RFCOMM_CONNINFO getsockopt handler accepts a socket that is not
connected as long as deferred setup is enabled:

	if (sk->sk_state != BT_CONNECTED &&
				!rfcomm_pi(sk)->dlc->defer_setup) {
		err = -ENOTCONN;
		break;
	}
	l2cap_sk = rfcomm_pi(sk)->dlc->session->sock->sk;

dlc->defer_setup is set in rfcomm_sock_init() when rfcomm_connect_ind()
creates a child socket for an incoming connection on a listening socket
that has BT_DEFER_SETUP enabled. It is never cleared afterwards. The
session, however, can go away underneath it.

rfcomm_recv_disc() forces the dlc state before tearing it down:

	d->state = BT_CLOSED;
	__rfcomm_dlc_close(d, err);

The RFCOMM_DEFER_SETUP early return in __rfcomm_dlc_close() only covers
BT_CONNECT, BT_CONFIG, BT_OPEN and BT_CONNECT2, so with the state
already BT_CLOSED that switch does not match and the function falls
through to rfcomm_dlc_unlink(), which sets d->session = NULL, while
d->defer_setup stays 1.

A getsockopt(SOL_RFCOMM, RFCOMM_CONNINFO) on the accepted socket after
that point therefore skips the -ENOTCONN path -- sk->sk_state is
BT_CLOSED, but dlc->defer_setup is still set -- and dereferences the
NULL session. No race is needed: once the DISC has been processed, the
dereference is unconditional.

Reproduced on a KASAN kernel under QEMU with a BR/EDR peer emulated over
/dev/vhci: the peer brings up an ACL link, opens L2CAP on the RFCOMM
PSM, starts a session and sends SABM for a channel bound with
BT_DEFER_SETUP, and sends DISC for that dlci after the socket has been
accepted. getsockopt(SOL_RFCOMM, RFCOMM_CONNINFO) on the accepted
socket then hits:

 Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
 0xdffffc0000000002: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI
 KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000010-0x0000000000000017]
 CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 150 Comm: init Tainted: G B 7.

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix create context out-of-bounds reads

smb2_parse_contexts() validates the complete create-context area but
does not limit each record to its Next field before dispatching it.  A
malformed chain can therefore expose bytes beyond the current context to
a handler.  The QFid handler also used a full response-structure cast
although it only reads DiskFileId.

The SMB2/SMB3 lease parsers made the same layout assumption: they read
LeaseState and LeaseFlags at canonical offsets rather than at
DataOffset.  A valid non-canonical DataOffset could therefore yield
unrelated in-bounds data, while a short DataLength was still accepted.

Limit each context to its Next value, reject offsets before the context
header, and reject malformed chains.  Bound the name range by the current
context and do not dispatch a known handler when DataLength is zero.  Read
the QFid DiskFileId only when the context data covers that field.  Parse the
lease context from DataOffset and require DataLength to match the v1 or v2
lease_context size used by ksmbd.  A size mismatch skips lease parsing
without failing the open.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: close handle after create-context parsing failure

SMB2_open() accounts a successful CREATE response as a remote open before
parsing its create contexts.  If smb2_parse_contexts() rejects malformed
context data, SMB2_open() returns without closing the handle, leaving the
server-side handle open and num_remote_opens elevated.

Close the handle after a post-CREATE context parsing failure so the error
path releases the remote resource and balances the open count.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: clean up failed cached directory opens

open_cached_dir() sends CREATE and QUERY_INFO as a compound request. If
the CREATE succeeds but a later command returns an error, the function
must retain the CREATE FID so common cleanup can issue SMB2_close(). It
also must not treat a response error as a valid CREATE.

Validate the CREATE response before using its fields, record the FIDs, and
mark the handle open before handling errors from later compound commands.
Move the -EREMCHG reconnect handling before response validation so a
missing response does not hide the reconnect request. Count the handle
when it is marked open; confirmed close responses decrement the counter,
while existing close retry behavior remains best effort on transport
failures.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: use finish_no_open() for non-regular inodes

An O_CREAT open can find an existing symlink or another non-regular
inode. cifs_atomic_open() calls finish_open() on it and attaches a
cifsFileInfo. Symlink inodes have no CIFS release operation, so the
dentry reference held by cifsFileInfo is leaked. FMODE_OPENED also
prevents the VFS from following the symlink.

Track whether cifs_do_create() returned an open server handle. For
non-regular inodes, close the handle if present, remove the pending
open, and call finish_no_open() so the VFS can continue the lookup.
Do not set FMODE_CREATED unless a regular file was opened. For
O_NOFOLLOW with __O_REGULAR, return -ELOOP before the VFS's
-EFTYPE check.

Defer closing a legacy POSIX handle on a non-regular inode until
after inode lookup. This avoids closing it again if lookup fails.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: close completed creates on compound wait errors

compound_send_recv() waits for responses in order. If a later wait is
interrupted, or if a later MID fails during response synchronization, an
earlier CREATE may already have opened a remote handle. The earlier mid
is then released without invoking handle_cancelled_mid(), leaving the
remote handle open because no FID was copied to the caller.

Mark completed earlier mids as cancelled when a compound wait or MID
synchronization aborts. Keep their response buffers attached while the
MIDs are synchronized, and transfer them only after synchronization of
the processed responses, so the release path can inspect successful
CREATE responses and queue SMB2_close() after a later failure. Account for
a remote open only after the close work is allocated and before it is
queued, since the caller has not yet updated num_remote_opens. Mark the
create+close compound used by smb2_unlink() so it is not closed again.
Non-CREATE responses and compounds that already include a close keep their
existing behavior.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: delete compound mids on send failure before unlock

When sending a compound request fails, smb_send_rqst() kicks off a
reconnect. compound_send_recv() still has those mids on pending_mid_q,
but it unlocks the server without removing them first.

During reconnect, cifs_abort_connection() walks pending_mid_q and runs
each mid callback. With no response yet, those callbacks return credits
and drop in_flight. Then compound_send_recv()'s send-error path returns
the same credits again. in_flight ends up decremented twice and
smb2_add_credits() WARNs.

syzbot hits this during SMB2_negotiate when the socket send fails.

cifs_call_async() already calls delete_mid() before unlock on send
failure. Do the same for compound chains and set cancelled_mid[] so the
out: path does not delete them again.

xfs: fix cursor and pointer handling when recovering iunlink buckets

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: act_ct: fix helper UAF due to extensions realloc

While calling the helpers, a raw pointer to the extensions area is
wired into expectations list:

  -> nf_ct_helper()
   -> helper->help()
    -> nf_ct_expect_related_report()
     -> nf_ct_expect_insert()
      -> hlist_add_head_rcu(&exp->lnode, &master_help->expectations)

In case the connection is not confirmed yet, more extensions can be
added afterwards with *_ext_add() calls reallocating the extension
space and leaving the now invalid pointer in the expectations list
that is later accessed while removing the expectation.

Make sure that helpers are called at the end after all the other
extensions are already added.

Note that the helper rejection now leaves the mark and labels set,
but that's not different from how the NAT was handled before or how
the mark and the labels were handled on confirmation failure.  And
there are no atomicity guarantees provided by the API anyway.

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: act_ct: avoid modifying shared unconfirmed ct entry

In a case where skb with an unconfirmed ct entry gets cloned, we may
end up processing both again but with different sets of extensions.

The series of events:

 1. The first clone wants to commit and runs the helpers wiring up
    the extension pointer into the expectation list.
 2. Then it looses the confirmation keeping the entry unconfirmed.
 3. Second clone now wants to commit labels or run NAT and adds the
    new extension for that breaking the pointer in the expectation
    list causing UAF on the destruction path later.

While this is possible to trigger, there should be no practical
network pipeline where we need to process both clones without
modifications in the same zone.  So, let's just reset the entry in
case for some reason we got an skb with a shared one.  This doesn't
affect any known use cases, but avoids any potential problems with
sharing and modification of the unconfirmed ct entry.

Unlike openvswitch module, act_ct allows for NAT without commit.
Changing that would be a uAPI break.  So, act_ct needs to reset on NAT
regardless of the commit flag to avoid reallocation of the extension
space.  This, however, doesn't really change the picture for sensible
networking cases as there should be no need to run the same packet
twice (before and after the clone) through conntrack without packet
header or zone changes and without commit.

The fixes tag points to the introduction of helpers, since that's the
main UAF trigger for the sharing.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: arm64: nv: Delay freeing of shadow S2 structures until VM destruction

We free the shadow S2 structures from kvm_arch_flush_shadow_all(), which
is a Bad Idea(tm). Freeing the page tables is fair game (this is what
this callback is for), but freeing the container that could still be
referenced by another part of the system is not great.

Instead, grow separate destructors that gets called when we tear the VM
down for good. From there, we can nuke both the individual MMUs as well
as the global array that points to them, safe in the knowledge that the
vcpus themselves have been destroyed already.

items.body:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: fix secure device page leak on uv_page_in() failure

In kvmppc_svm_page_in(), if uv_page_in() fails after
kvmppc_uvmem_get_page() has succeeded, the secure device page is never
released.  kvmppc_uvmem_get_page() sets a bit in kvmppc_uvmem_bitmap,
allocates a kvmppc_uvmem_page_pvt struct, marks the GFN as
KVMPPC_GFN_UVMEM_PFN, and calls zone_device_page_init() which sets
refcount=1 and locks the page.  The subsequent goto out_finalize skips
the *mig.dst assignment, so migrate_vma_finalize() is a no-op for the
page, and none of those resources are ever reclaimed.

Each occurrence permanently consumes one entry from the firmware-bounded
secure memory pool (kvmppc_uvmem_bitmap), leaks pvt, and leaves the GFN
marked as secure — making it unusable for the lifetime of the VM.

The twin __kvmppc_svm_page_out() already handles the analogous uv_page_out()
failure correctly with unlock_page(dpage); __free_page(dpage).  Apply
the same pattern here: unlock_page() followed by put_page(), which
chains through free_zone_device_folio() into kvmppc_uvmem_folio_free()
to clear the bitmap bit, free pvt, and reset the GFN state.

Reachable whenever uv_page_in() returns an error (e.g. UV pool
exhaustion) on any POWER9/10 + Ultravisor/PEF system.

Attackers can upload a bundle whose sub-agent uses an absolute or parent-traversing working directory, bypassing root-only validation in bundles.py, to read and write host files as the runner user.

items.title: CVE-2026-112014 - LobsterAI before 2026.10.16 contains a hardcoded password vulnerability that all...
items.body: LobsterAI before 2026.10.16 contains a hardcoded password vulnerability that allows attackers to decrypt exported provider API keys encrypted with the constant 'lobsterai-APP'. Attackers who obtain a providers export file can derive the AES-GCM key via PBKDF2 using the embedded salt and recover every third-party AI provider API key.

items.title: CVE-2026-112013 - libtta through 2.3 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability in tta_decoder_init_g...
items.body: libtta through 2.3 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability in tta_decoder_init_get_info() that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying an unvalidated zero sample rate. Attackers can craft a .tta file with a recomputed header CRC32 that triggers SIGFPE, crashing applications including the bundled tta console tool.

items.title: CVE-2026-112012 - libtta through 2.3 contains a stack out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability i...
items.body: libtta through 2.3 contains a stack out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability in tta_decoder_process_stream() and tta_decoder_process_frame() because header checks never reject a zero channel count. Attackers can supply a crafted .tta file declaring zero channels so decorrelation accesses cache[-1] with stream-derived values, corrupting stack memory in decoding applications.

items.title: CVE-2026-112011 - libtta through 2.3 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in tta_decoder_ini...
items.body: libtta through 2.3 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in tta_decoder_init_get_info() that allows attackers to cause a heap buffer overflow on 32-bit builds via unvalidated header fields. Attackers can supply a crafted .tta file with a sample rate of 1 and large samples value, wrapping the seek table allocation and crashing applications.

items.title: CVE-2026-112010 - smpeg through 2.0.0 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in stream_header...
items.body: smpeg through 2.0.0 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in stream_header() in MPEGsystem.cpp that allows attackers to wrap packet_size by declaring an undersized packet length. Attackers can supply a crafted MPEG file opened via SMPEG_new, SMPEG_new_rwops or SMPEG_new_data to trigger a reachable assertion or out-of-bounds copy, crashing the application.

items.title: CVE-2026-112009 - smpeg through 2.0.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in MPEGsyst...
items.body: smpeg through 2.0.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in MPEGsystem::FillBuffer() that allows attackers to read past the 16384-byte buffer by supplying a crafted system header stream table. Attackers can provide an MPEG file whose stream table bytes all set the high bit, which crashes applications opening it through SMPEG_new, SMPEG_new_rwops, or SMPEG_new_data.

items.title: CVE-2026-112008 - libmng through 2.0.3 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in mng_...
items.body: libmng through 2.0.3 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in mng_read_ordr() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory because ORDR entry buffers are sized by 5-byte on-wire records instead of 8-byte in-memory entries. Attackers can supply a crafted MNG file with MHDR, DHDR and a multi-record ORDR chunk to applications calling mng_read or mng_readdisplay, writing attacker-controlled data past the allocation and crashing the application.

items.title: CVE-2026-112007 - Schism Tracker through 20260524 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerabilit...
items.body: Schism Tracker through 20260524 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in fmt_ult_load_song() in fmt/ult.c that fails to clamp the one-byte sample count to MAX_SAMPLES. Attackers can supply a crafted .ult module that overwrites the instruments pointer array, causing csf_destroy() to free attacker-chosen pointers and crash the application.

items.title: CVE-2026-112006 - OpenTelemetry opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http 1.5.0 before 1.45.0 contain...
items.body: OpenTelemetry opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http 1.5.0 before 1.45.0 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability that disables TLS verification when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE variables are empty strings. Man-in-the-middle attackers can impersonate the collector to read or alter exported traces, metrics, and logs, including authentication headers from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS.

items.title: CVE-2026-112005 - WhoDB 0.104.0 before 0.135.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows...
items.body: WhoDB 0.104.0 before 0.135.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows remote attackers to read and write arbitrary host files by running DuckDB filesystem functions through the query editor. Attackers can log in to a DuckDB file without credentials and use read_text, read_blob, COPY ... TO or ATTACH to steal session.key and stored database credentials or overwrite files.

items.title: CVE-2026-112004 - Teable before 2026-10-12T12-45-53Z.3331 contains an authorization bypass vulnera...
items.body: Teable before 2026-10-12T12-45-53Z.3331 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to rename folders in other bases by supplying a foreign folderId. The PATCH /api/base/:baseId/node/folder/:folderId endpoint checks base|update only against the URL baseId, so attackers can rename folders in bases where they lack membership.

items.title: CVE-2026-112003 - ProjectSend 2.0.0 before 2.7.0 contains a path validation flaw in OrphanFileScan...
items.body: ProjectSend 2.0.0 before 2.7.0 contains a path validation flaw in OrphanFileScanner::isOrphan() that allows staff with import_orphans permission to treat tracked files as orphans. Attackers can submit ./ path aliases to the orphans import or delete endpoints, deleting or adopting other owners' files while bypassing delete_others_files.

items.title: CVE-2026-112002 - ProjectSend 2.5.0 before 2.7.0 contains an unverified password change vulnerabil...
items.body: ProjectSend 2.5.0 before 2.7.0 contains an unverified password change vulnerability in PasswordController::update() that lets sessions of Social-provisioned accounts set local passwords without the current password. Attackers holding a stolen session cookie can send PUT /settings/password to create a durable local password, enroll their own second factor, and persistently take over the account.

items.title: CVE-2026-112001 - ProjectSend 2.0.0 before 2.7.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability...
items.body: ProjectSend 2.0.0 before 2.7.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows restricted API token holders to change the token owner's credentials via PATCH /api/v1/users/{user}. Attackers with a token limited to manage_users and edit_users can set a new owner password, clear two-factor authentication, and sign in interactively with the owner's full role permissions.

items.title: CVE-2026-112000 - Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the ...
items.body: Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the gateway that allows any authenticated user to call Subscribe, Ack, and unregistered methods without permission checks. Attackers can supply another tenant's subscription ID to Subscribe to hijack it, read and acknowledge its events, starve the legitimate consumer, and enumerate cluster users via ListUser.

items.title: CVE-2026-111999 - Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that a...
items.body: Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to publish events to any eventbus through the gateway CloudEvents HTTP receiver. Attackers can send forged CloudEvents to the /namespaces/{ns}/eventbus/{name}/events or legacy /gateway/{name} paths, bypassing token authentication and authPublish checks, so they are stored and delivered to subscription sinks.

items.title: CVE-2026-111998 - Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contains a default credentials vulnerability that allo...
items.body: Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contains a default credentials vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain cluster-admin access by using the hardcoded admin token. Attackers can send the fixed Bearer token to the gateway gRPC proxy port to manage namespaces, eventbuses, users, tokens, and role bindings, and read or publish events.
